title: Tor bounds descend from bounded flat local models
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\Gamma$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $\Gamma_T=p_T^*\Gamma$ for schemes $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $Q\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Gamma_S))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $\{g_i:V_i\to S\}_{i=1}^n$ is a finite covering family of $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-site]. Fix integers $r\le s$ and cochain complexes $L_i^\bullet$ of $\Gamma_{V_i}$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], with $L_i^q=0$ for $q\notin[r,s]$, all terms flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and isomorphisms $g_i^*Q\simeq L_i^\bullet$ in the derived category. Then for every $\Gamma_S$-module $N$ placed in degree zero,
$$g_i^*(Q\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Gamma_S}N)\simeq L_i^\bullet\otimes_{\Gamma_{V_i}}g_i^*N.$$
Here $g_i^*$ is the exact inverse-image functor with the pulled-back coefficient ring. The tensor on the right is ordinary tensor of complexes. Moreover $H^q(Q\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Gamma_S}N)=0$ for every $q\notin[r,s]$ and every $N$. Equivalently, $Q$ has Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$ [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude].

proof.text: Convert the given sectionwise flatness to two-sided internal tensor flatness using InternalAbelianSheafModule.flat_iff_sectionModule [lem-c2-internal-section-module-flatness]. The support bounds give IsStrictlyGE r and IsStrictlyLE s; apply the existing generic source bounded-flat K-flat criterion CochainComplex.kFlat_of_bounded_of_flat [lem-sfb-bounded-above-flat-kflat] to each L_i. No flatness of the test module N is required.

For F_i = CondensedRing.upperStar Γ.X g_i, the coefficient isomorphism [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] makes F_i exact. Use its existing leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory to pass between total derived inverse image and termwise inverse image. Compose leftDerivedUpperStarTensorIso, the existing module-object tensor-pullback comparison of [new-proetale-derived-module-pullback-monoidal], with these exactness comparisons and the single-functor comparison F_i(N[0]) ≅ F_i(N)[0]. Substitute the supplied model F_i(Q) ≅ Q(L_i). This gives F_i(Q tensor-derived N[0]) ≅ Q(L_i) tensor-derived F_i(N)[0].

Use the already proved generic source declaration DerivedCategory.QObjTensorSingleFunctorObjIso [lem-weil-pbc-source-kflat-tensor-single-model], specialized to the internal module category and F_i(N). Compose with Q applied to the inverse of CochainComplex.mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso to identify its termwise tensor model with the ordinary total tensor complex L_i tensor F_i(N)[0] [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. This proves the first conclusion. For cohomology bounds, the generic proved source theorem DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn_Q_obj_of_flat [lem-trf-source-bounded-flat-tor-amplitude] applies to the same support and flatness hypotheses. Transport its Tor-test bound along the derived local tensor comparison of step 2. This avoids re-elaborating the total-complex comparison in the vanishing argument.

Let H be H^q(Q tensor-derived N[0]) for q outside [r,s]. The exact-functor comparison mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] and the local tensor isomorphism identify every F_i(H) with the zero local homology object. Package the finite family as a Scheme.Cover. Apply the public derived zero-object detection in [lem-zl-condensed-cover-restriction-conservative] to H[0]: mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor identifies each restriction with F_i(H)[0], which is zero. Hence H[0] is zero. Full faithfulness of the derived single functor gives H=0. Private helpers perform this descent for an abstract module and abstract derived object so specialization does not unfold concrete tensor constructions. This includes empty covers. Finally apply the two derived t-structure vanishing criteria to obtain Tor amplitude [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude].
